newsitem.title: CROATIA: Some Croatia rail strikers cave in, resume services.
newsitem.headline: Some Croatia rail strikers cave in, resume services.

text.p: Some striking railway workers in Croatia caved in on Saturday and returned to work a day after state railway company HZ threatened to sack them if they continued their protest for higher wages, HZ said.

A spokesman for Croatian railways said that some domestic services had resumed, including the busy route between Zagreb and the southern Adriatic city of Split and between Zagreb and the eastern town of Vinkovci.
Most workers, however, ignored government calls to go back to work and went on strike for the third day, halting most services apart from international and some cargo trains.
HZ said it was losing 1.6 million kuna ($300,000) a day and urged about 11,000 striking workers to give up their protest, accusing them of damaging the country's economy.

"By not heeding our calls, strike leaders still insist on their primary aim -- to cause chaos and the greatest possible damage to the entire Croatian economy," HZ said in a statement carried by state news agency HINA.
"The management is again telling the strikers they should give up. There is nothing to negotiate," the statement said.
Strikers accused HZ's management of drawing up blacklists of employees it planned to lay off. HZ said that some strikers were intimidating workers to stop them from returning to work.
